reviewedContracts: Each mounted RetainedStageMaterial owns its own MeshPhysicalMaterial, including components instantiated from the reused access ReactElement; no global shared mutable finished material was introduced.
Construction attaches its original raw material. The finished primitive is detached but not automatically disposed by R3F; the owner releases it on a true material-key change or component cleanup.

Finished child material properties and shader callbacks are forwarded unchanged. Existing shader descriptors, geometry factories and shader constants match the fixed parent source in the targeted AST audit.
Water is lazy until first shown, then remains mounted but hidden. Both reflection submission and animated uniform updates return immediately when inactive.
Resuming water invalidates the reflection cache before subsequent capture; existing render-target cleanup, renderer-state restoration and ripple reference counting remain intact.
Material disposal does not dispose shared external texture maps; existing texture ownership remains with their current loaders/resource owners.
No network path, personal-data handling, credential access or security boundary was added by these three runtime files.
limitations: The21-check hook harness uses deterministic React/renderer stubs, not the real R3F reconciler or StrictMode effect replay. It proves its stated ownership/pause/resume contracts, not complete runtime behavior.

The immediate effect cleanup can dispose a retained material during DEV StrictMode effect replay. Three materials can be reinitialized by the renderer afterward, so this is a possible DEV recompilation concern, not a demonstrated production correctness defect. No unrelated StrictMode rewrite is justified by this review.
The source AST comparison proves exact authored property/constants equality, not rendered image equality or full shader-program lifecycle equivalence.
